questions.questionText: Which of the following statements best defines Docker and its purpose for developers?
options: Docker is a platform that uses containers to package applications and their dependencies, allowing them to run consistently across different environments.
Docker is a cloud storage service for backing up code repositories.
Docker is a programming language used to write microservices.
Docker is a hardware virtualization tool that creates full virtual machines.
questions.correctAnswer: Docker is a platform that uses containers to package applications and their dependencies, allowing them to run consistently across different environments.
questions.explanation: Docker provides containerization, letting developers bundle an app with all required libraries and settings into a lightweight, portable container that runs the same on any host system, which simplifies development, testing, and deployment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following options correctly lists three Docker commands discussed in the lecture and describes their primary functions?
options: docker -v (shows Docker version), docker pull (downloads an image from Docker Hub), docker images (lists locally stored images)
docker start (starts a stopped container), docker commit (saves container changes as an image), docker rm (removes a container)
docker login (authenticates with Docker Hub), docker tag (adds a tag to an image), docker inspect (displays detailed information about an object)
docker build (creates an image from a Dockerfile), docker push (uploads an image to Docker Hub), docker exec (runs a command in a running container)
questions.correctAnswer: docker -v (shows Docker version), docker pull (downloads an image from Docker Hub), docker images (lists locally stored images)
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly covered the commands docker -v to display the Docker version, docker pull to fetch an image from Docker Hub, and docker images to list the images available locally.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sequences correctly outlines the Docker workflow for moving a Node.js application from machine A to machine B as described in the lecture?
options: Create a Dockerfile, build the image on machine A, export the image as a tar file, transfer the tar to machine B, load the image, and run a container.
Package the Node.js app into a zip file, transfer it to machine B, unzip, and execute with node without using Docker.
Write a Dockerfile, copy the Node.js source to machine B, build the image on machine B, run the container directly without pushing.
Create a Dockerfile, build the image on machine A, push the image to a registry, pull the image on machine B, and run a container.
questions.correctAnswer: Create a Dockerfile, build the image on machine A, push the image to a registry, pull the image on machine B, and run a container.
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes bundling the application into a Docker image on machine A, sharing that image via a registry (push/pull), and then creating a container on machine B. Option 1 follows this exact sequence, whereas the other options either omit the registry step or avoid Docker entirely.
